fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Secret Spells of Everyday English", "body": "Chance opens with the word animal, suggesting its roots can read as bad spirit, and Laurel calls this kind of play anagrammatology. She then walks through what she calls the secret spells of the English language, the way we describe an ordinary day: waking in mourning, going off to earn a living, calling our jobs undertakings and ending up with a weak end. She pairs pray with prey, prophet with profit and worship with warship, and argues that words like these quietly send people in the wrong direction. Her remedy is to navigate by the heart, which she calls the compass of compassion."}, {"title": "Green Language and Soul Harmonics", "body": "Asked about green language and the language of the birds, Laurel describes a collective project rather than an invented tongue: no one person can impose a new language, she says, but many people speaking with the same high intention can tune English until it uplifts whoever hears it. She compares good conversation to energetic acupuncture, two people amplifying each other like batteries. Chance answers with his own idea of soul harmonics, the sense that two people talking openly create harmony or dissonance like two notes on a guitar, with imagination supplying insights neither had alone. He says that realization is what led him into podcasting."}, {"title": "Rhyme, Memory and Imagination", "body": "Chance asks how Laurel memorizes her pieces, and she describes rhyme as an electro-poetic force, coupling a big idea with a sound of several meanings until it plays over and over in her head like magnets finding their balance. She then performs Word Fire, a piece she says nobody had heard, including the line that a heavy heart must be gold. Chance ties that gold to authenticity through its chemical symbol, Au. Asked what imagination is, Laurel hears I'm a genie inside the word and notes that imagine and enigma mirror each other, since it takes imagination to solve an enigma."}, {"title": "Omnificence and the Question of Control", "body": "Laurel shares omnificent, a word she found in a dictionary meaning possessing full creative power, and argues that a species which has already shown its full destructive power must hold the creative side too. Chance offers imaginal cells turning a caterpillar into a butterfly as a picture of human change, and Laurel urges him to make it a children's book. When Chance asks whether an architecture of control lives in language, Laurel answers in verse: some propaganda was surely implanted, she says, but like sounds also gather naturally, and the hypnosis is reversible. On non-human interference she says she does her best not to go there."}, {"title": "Taking Command of the English Language", "body": "Laurel summarizes her anthem Taking Command of the English Language in verse, arguing that English is the leading software of the Western mind, carrying biases she likens to computer viruses and says the church promulgated as mind control. Her fix is participatory: words others have offered, such as hallow in place of hello and greatfulness, and a planned literary lotto on her Word Magic Global forum. She cites Confucius on correcting language first and explains kotodama as the recognition that words have spirits. In his closing, Chance shares his own forum entry, borning for the start of the day, and invites artists and musicians to collaborate with her."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Get the wax out of your third ear and prepare to expand your vocabulary with the secret spells of the English language! In this conversation, poet and punster Laurel Airica is going to teach us about the magic in everyday words. Here you will hear a fascinating foray into the metaphysics of your mouth-sounds!
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Affectionately known as the metaphysical mother goose, Laurel reveals occult meanings hidden before our eyes as unconsciously uttered linguistic white lies. And by exposing the programs inserted in the sentences that make up our lives, she has helped many magical beings break free of language slavery and put spirit back in its place in our hearts and our words.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Mean, dogma and the church in our words", "body": "Laurel Airica argues that English absorbed the dominant consciousness of the church when it formed as a melting pot of other tongues, so a universe divided between warring powers, a fallen humanity, the misery of life and the inferiority of women all sit inside everyday words. She points to the two forms of prey and profit behind the so called holy wars and to the many meanings of mean, from cruel to average. Turning dogma around, she finds am God, and the talk turns to the golden mean and to Chance Garton's point that the perfectly average person never actually exists."}, {"title": "Two eyes in the alphabet", "body": "Laurel's Book of E, a free e-book of alphabet alchemy, reads original sin as original syn, the synchrony between us and whatever generated us. Chance contrasts the lowercase i, its dot floating apart from the bar like an all seeing eye, with the capital I and the letter y as shapes of union that bridge two worlds. Laurel answers with her poem about feeling like a little i one moment and towering like a capital I the next, and Chance hears the quest inside the question, suggesting that knowing who you are means asking that question again and again."}, {"title": "The lie in alive", "body": "Chance names the fear of death as the primary fear of our world and calls the notion that someday you will no longer be the lie hidden inside being alive. Laurel adds that a lie is not fully alive because it carries no vital energy and so cannot endure. She recommends the book Whitley Strieber wrote with his late wife Anne, books on trees, birds and the octopus, and the Three Principles of Sydney Banks. Turning to Freud's pleasure principle, she says he got stuck on the lower chakras, while Chance proposes beauty as the only solid foundation for a philosophy."}, {"title": "From humankind to human kindness", "body": "Laurel offers her platinum rule, that we do unto ourselves as we do unto others, and calls our next evolutionary step a move from humankind to human kindness. Heart and earth share the same letters, she observes, and the purpose of life is not to get ahead but to get a heart. Putting our ear to the earth and listening to the heart makes us an oracle, a word shared by the soothsayer, the outer edge of the ear and the chambers of the heart. Chance, delighted, names the heart a third ear to match the third eye between the brows."}, {"title": "Asking for inspiration", "body": "Asked how she moves past creative blocks, Laurel says she has long invited Archangel Uriel, whom she read is the archangel of language and culture, to co create with her, and later learned Uriel is said to have gifted the Kabbalah. Chance links this to asking the question instead of saying I don't know, and to his friend Richard Sacks of Lost Arts Radio, who likens the mind to a child that helps once it is invited into a game. Laurel shares words she has found and coined, from beautiful as be you to full to nemosophist, a lover of the forest, and turns word into world with one L."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I call it the platinum rule, which is we do unto ourselves as we do unto others. It cannot be otherwise.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "I believe our essential evolutionary transition now is meant to be from humankind to human kindness.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "Sometimes I like to say that God created planet earth so the word could be heard.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "When we put our ear to the earth and listen to our heart, we become an oracle.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "Don't take words at face value. Look into that face. See what other words you find in it.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "A lie is not fully alive. It doesn't have vital energy.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "Just as we have two eyes in our face, there are also two eyes in the alphabet.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "Any philosophy that doesn't have beauty as its foundation is pretty much on shaky ground.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}, {"text": "We have a third eye in between our eyes and the forehead and we have a third ear in our chest with our heart.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}, {"text": "The words you use can be that very thing, and you can change the words and change your life.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The thing to do is to navigate via the heart because we each have the built-in compass in the heart. It is the compass of compassion.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "We could create a chorus of beautiful music through our social intercourse with a language that has been so tuned up that when we speak to each other, we're uplifting each other.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "The imagination is what creates that extra new awareness or insight that you reached when talking to this other person that you never had before.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}, {"text": "If your heart is heavy, it must be gold.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "It's often been said enlightenment is a destructive process and what that really means is getting out of our own way.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}, {"text": "People sometimes say, \"Well, I'm not creative.\" But, as a species, we've already demonstrated that we possess full destructive power. So, the other side has to be true as well.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "English is the leading software of the Western mind and it's filled with cultural biases that are akin to computer viruses that infect our thinking.", "author": "Laurel Airica", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/86c5f55a-0964-4bbc-916d-e5bb3a6a9bef/laurel-airica/orig.jpg"}, {"text": "I think it's a good idea that we start investing more intention into this meme magic that is possible to ignite things for good or ill in people's mass consciousness almost overnight.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.innerversepodcast.com/sq/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/chance-garton-patreon-portrait/orig.png"}]
